The variant is SA insured unemployment from regular state programs, not NSA state totals and not all-program continued weeks claimed."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened the DOL ETA UI Weekly Claims archive and publication schedule page.","result":"The DOL page says the UI Weekly Claims News Release is published each week on Thursday at 8:30 AM EST, lists Wednesday November 25, 2026 as the 2026 non-Thursday exception, and shows the page was updated July 9, 2026. For the continued-claims week ending July 11, 2026, the first Thursday release after the normal two-week lag is July 23, 2026."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened the current DOL UI Weekly Claims news release PDF dated July 9, 2026.","result":"The release reports advance seasonally adjusted insured unemployment of 1,814,000 for the week ending June 27, 2026, up 8,000 from the revised 1,806,000 for June 20, with a four-week average of 1,808,000."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Read the DOL seasonally adjusted weekly claims history table in the same July 9, 2026 release.","result":"Recent SA insured unemployment values were 1,786,000 for May 30, 1,800,000 for June 6, 1,812,000 for June 13, 1,806,000 for June 20, and 1,814,000 for June 27; the comparable June 28, 2025 value was 1,952,000."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"history.lookup","call":"Opened FRED CCSA as a public history mirror for DOL ETA continued claims.","result":"FRED CCSA shows 2026-06-27 at 1,814,000, 2026-06-20 at 1,806,000, 2026-06-13 at 1,812,000, 2026-06-06 at 1,800,000, and 2026-05-30 at 1,786,000, updated July 9, 2026 7:34 AM CDT, with next release date July 16, 2026."},{"kind":"text","text":"Reference class and base rate: for one- to two-week-ahead SA continued-claims forecasts, the strongest base rate is persistence in the recent DOL SA level plus the recent average weekly change. The last five published levels rose from 1.786 million to 1.814 million, but initial claims for July 4 were 215,000 and the four-week initial-claims average was 218,750, so the near-term pressure is mild rather than a breakout."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior = latest official SA insured unemployment of 1.814 million; historical sample = 53 fetched weekly changes from the DOL table, June 28, 2025 through June 27, 2026; adjustment components = +0.010 million for two weeks of modest recent upward momentum, 0.000 million for policy mechanics because no Extended Benefits trigger was on, and 0.000 million for variant conversion because all anchors use the same SA insured-unemployment variant. Point = 1.814 + 0.010 = 1.824 million. For the fetched weekly changes, sigma = 0.0208 million, so one-week 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 0.0266 million. Because the target is two unpublished weeks ahead, I scale by sqrt(2), giving about 0.0376 million, rounded to 0.038 million; interval = 1.824 +/- 0.038 = [1.786, 1.862] million."},{"kind":"text","text":"Level and momentum effects: the latest 1.814 million is above the May 30 level by 0.028 million but still below the comparable prior-year value of 1.952 million. Momentum argues for a small increase, while the latest initial-claims easing to 215,000 limits the upward adjustment."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk would come from a delayed follow-through from late-June layoffs or seasonal-adjustment miss that lifts continued claims above 1.862 million. Downside risk would come from faster exits from UI rolls or lower July initial claims that pull the print below 1.786 million. A holiday-week reporting distortion or a large state-level administrative revision would be the main outside the interval scenario."},{"kind":"forecast","point":1.824,"ciLow":1.786,"ciHigh":1.862}]}
